Row 30, concurrency: the key-value layer against auth-framework's own PostgreSQL SQL, 8 concurrent workers (same harness, CONC=8)

Measured: 2026-11-24 (after 02:30Z), branch chore/portfolio-pin on main e1ca6b9 (0.18.35) plus the example (CONC env var added).
Rerun:    PERSISTANT_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... CONC=8 PAIRS=30 cargo run -q --release -p persistant-sqlx --example pg_vs_auth_sql
Where:    same as bench/pg-vs-auth-sql.txt (Windows 11 laptop, postgres:16 in Docker, loopback, 2000 rows). Pool of 16 connections shared by 8 workers
          (join! on one thread), each worker 25 calls per side per pair; datum = per-pair ratio of time per call (throughput), persistant/direct.
Load:     NOT quiet (about 20 claude processes, 5 cargo/rustc, host CPU often 97 to 100 percent; per-pair values in the raw lines below).
          The quiet-box rerun asked for by the PM TASK could not be had: the box was not quiet at any point I looked.

Result (n = 30 pairs each, ratio persistant/direct)
op              median  p25    p75    min    max
Token check     1.96    1.89   2.02   1.83   2.12   about 2x, same as one connection: two statements against one
Session read    1.03    0.98   1.08   0.92   1.11   parity
Kv get          1.01    0.99   1.04   0.90   1.12   parity
Store token     10.57   10.19  10.72  7.26   11.74  NOT the 2.9x of one connection: about 10x, tight IQR. UNEXPLAINED here (a hypothesis only: the
                                                    layer's batch holds a transaction across several statements, which serialises on the pool; not tested)
control_same    1.02    0.99   1.04   0.90   1.17   centres on 1, IQR 0.05 (tighter than the 0.64 of the one-connection run)
control_slow    0.43    0.39   0.61   0.34   0.87   the harness sees a 2 ms slowdown

Not measured: why store scales badly (a profile or pg_stat_activity run would say), other worker counts, a request mix. Raw lines follow.
